title: Falling ball

reference.basis: No object of known size is visible in the plane of the motion.

slow_motion.evidence: No caption, narration, or visual cue indicates slow motion.

subjects.description: Small round teal object falling vertically from top to floor.

observation.what_happens: A small teal ball drops from just below a black-and-white striped bar near the top of the frame. It falls vertically down to the brown floor, ending when it contacts the floor.

calibration.note: scale from the fall itself: 4365 px/s² over 8 arcs = g of 9.807 m/s²

given: g = 9.807 m/s² (Earth); it set the scale, so treat g as known and fixed
reasoning: x moves steadily forward while y falls and rebounds with shrinking height and period, the classic bouncing ball with horizontal drift. g is given and fixed the scale, floor level and restitution are unknown. Candidates keep the same bounce event and differ only in air drag: none vs linear vs quadratic to test if air matters on Earth.

law.summary: The ball flies like in vacuum and bounces off the floor losing the same fraction of speed each time.

caveats: Early frames show a few large outliers likely from detection, not physics.
Sideways position wavers slightly, suggesting tiny jitter rather than real force.
Air drag was tried and fit to nothing, so vacuum is fine here.
critique.finding: The ball drops freely under gravity and bounces off the floor keeping {e} of its speed. The floor sits at {y_floor} below the start.
critique.headline: The ball falls freely and bounces cleanly off the floor.
critique.why_it_won: It includes the bounce off the floor while the plain fall without a bounce misses badly and adding air drag changes nothing.

headline: The ball falls freely and bounces cleanly off the floor.
finding: The ball drops freely under gravity and bounces off the floor keeping 0.74956 ± 0.00016 of its speed. The floor sits at -1.0707 ± 0.0028 m below the start.

eyeball.law_in_words: Ballistic free fall under constant gravity with vertical position y(t)=y0+vy0*t-0.5*g*t^2 and horizontal constant velocity, with floor contact reversing normal velocity as v_after = -e*v_before.
